\noindent   \textbf{Question 1.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Discuss the situations under which rank correlation is used. Establish the formula for Spearman's rank correlation when ranks are untied. Obtain the limits of the rank correlation coefficient.
  \item Prove that the coefficient of correlation is zero when two random variables are independent, and show also by giving an example that the converse is not true. Let $r$ be the coefficient of correlation between two random variables $X$ and $Y$. Show that:
    $$r = \frac{\sigma_x^2 + \sigma_y^2 - \sigma_{x-y}^2}{2\sigma_x \sigma_y}$$
    where $\sigma_x^2$, $\sigma_y^2$, and $\sigma_{x-y}^2$ are the variances of the random variables $X$, $Y$, and $X - Y$ respectively.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 2.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Differentiate between correlation and regression. If $(X_i, Y_i), i = 1, 2, \dots, n$ are pairs of observations, then find the constants $a$ and $b$ of the line $Y = a + bX$ by the least squares method.
  \item Let $Y_e$ be the predicted value of $Y$ from the regression line of $Y$ on $X$ and $e_i = Y_i - Y_{ei}$ be the error. Show that the variance of error is $V(e) = \sigma_y^2(1 - r^2)$, where $\sigma_y^2$ is the variance of $Y$ and $r$ is the coefficient of correlation between $X$ and $Y$.
  \item Let $2Y - X + 3 = 0$ be the regression line of $Y$ on $X$ and its angle with the regression line of $X$ on $Y$ is $45^\circ$. Obtain the regression coefficient corresponding to the line of $X$ on $Y$ and the correlation coefficient $r$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 3.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define partial correlation. In case of three variables $X_1$, $X_2$, $X_3$, show that:
    $$r_{12.3} = \frac{r_{12} - r_{13}r_{23}}{\sqrt{(1 - r_{13}^2)(1 - r_{23}^2)}}$$
  \item Let the random variable $X$ have the marginal density:
    $$f(x) = \frac{1}{2}, \quad -1 < x < 1$$
    and $0$ otherwise. Let the conditional density of $Y$ given $X=x$ be:
    $$f(y|x) = 
\begin{cases} 1 &  \text{if } x < y < x + 1, \quad -1 < x < 0 \\ 1 &  \text{if } -x < y < 1 - x, \quad 0 \le x < 1 \end{cases}$$
    Show that the variables $X$ and $Y$ are uncorrelated.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 4.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define Poisson distribution. Derive the Poisson distribution as a limiting case of the binomial distribution.
  \item Let $X \sim P(\lambda_1)$ and $Y \sim P(\lambda_2)$ be two independent Poisson random variables. Find the probability distribution of $X + Y$, and find $P(X + Y > 0)$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 5.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Differentiate between binomial and hypergeometric distributions.
  \item A bag contains 3 defective and 4 good items. 3 items are chosen randomly from the bag one by one. If $X$ denotes the number of defective items drawn, write the probability distribution of $X$ under the situations of:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item with replacement,
      \item without replacement.
    \end{parts}
    Show that the probability of selection of a defective item remains the same at each draw in both cases of selection.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 6.}

\begin{parts}
  \item What is meant by attribute? Define the term class, class frequency, and order of class. Given that $(AB) = 150$, $(Aeta) = 230$, $(\alpha B) = 260$, and $(\alpha) = 2340$, find the rest of the frequencies and check the independence of attributes $A$ and $B$.
  \item Let $X$ be a binomial variate with parameters $n$ and $p$. Obtain the moment generating function of $X$, and show that $E(X/n) = p$ and $Var(X/n) = \frac{p(1-p)}{n}$.
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 7.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define negative binomial distribution. Obtain the mean and variance of the negative binomial distribution.
  \item Define uniform distribution in the continuous case. Obtain its mean and variance. The occurrence time of buses at a stop has a uniform distribution with mean arrival time 2 minutes and variance $4/3$ minutes. What is the probability that a person will wait at least 3 minutes for a bus?
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 8.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Write the probability density function of the normal distribution. Let $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$. Obtain the moment generating function of $X$.
  \item State and prove Chebyshev's inequality. If for a random variable $X$, $P(|X - 2| < 4) \ge \frac{21}{25}$, then find the mean and variance of $X$ using Chebyshev's inequality.
  \item Define Beta distribution and find its mean and variance.
  \item Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent random variables from:
    
\begin{parts}
      \item Binomial distribution, i.e., $X \sim B(n_1, p)$ and $Y \sim B(n_2, p)$,
      \item Poisson distribution, i.e., $X \sim P(\lambda_1)$ and $Y \sim P(\lambda_2)$.
    \end{parts}
    Recognize the conditional distribution of $(X=x \mid X+Y=t)$ in each case.
\end{parts}
